name: Maya
profile: Maya is an 11-year-old with significant communication challenges. She is non-speaking and uses a communication device inconsistently. Maya has strong sensory-seeking behaviours and often engages in repetitive movements. She demonstrates clear preferences and dislikes but struggles to communicate these effectively, leading to frustration and occasional aggressive behaviours when needs are unmet.
challenges: Limited functional communication resulting in unmet needs
Aggressive behaviours (hitting, biting) during high frustration
Staff uncertainty about how to interpret and respond to behaviours
goals: Increase functional communication for basic needs and preferences
Reduce aggressive incidents through improved communication
Increase engagement in structured learning activities
Support staff in understanding and responding to Maya's communication

recommendedEBPs.title: Functional Communication Training
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Teaches Maya alternative communication methods to replace aggression

recommendedEBPs.title: Augmentative & Alternative Communication
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Provides consistent, accessible communication system suited to Maya's needs

recommendedEBPs.title: Functional Behaviour Assessment
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Identifies what Maya is communicating through aggressive behaviours

recommendedEBPs.title: Naturalistic Intervention
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Embeds communication teaching in naturally occurring activities and routines

recommendedEBPs.title: Reinforcement
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Systematically reinforces communication attempts to increase frequency

implementation.functionalCommunication: Staff identified that hitting often communicated 'I need space' or 'This is too hard'. Maya was taught to hand over a 'break' card or push away materials as alternative communication.
implementation.aacSystem: Speech therapist simplified Maya's device to 12 core words and added tactile symbols for key preferences. Staff modelled device use throughout the day.
implementation.behaviourAssessment: Detailed ABC (Antecedent-Behaviour-Consequence) data revealed aggression was most common during loud, busy activities and when demands exceeded Maya's capacity.
implementation.naturalisticTeaching: Staff embedded communication teaching into snack time, transitions, and play, rather than isolated 'communication sessions'.
implementation.reinforcement: When Maya used device, cards, or gestures to communicate, staff responded immediately and enthusiastically, reinforcing the communication.

outcomes: Aggressive incidents reduced from 12 per week to 2 per week over 10 weeks
Maya now consistently uses 'break' card and pushes materials away to communicate needs
Device use increased from 3 times daily to 15+ times daily
Maya participated in full group art activity for first time, using device to request materials
Staff report feeling more confident in understanding and responding to Maya
reflections: The functional behaviour assessment was crucial - it shifted staff perspective from 'Maya is aggressive' to 'Maya is communicating distress'. Teaching alternatives only worked because staff committed to responding immediately and positively to all communication attempts. Simplifying the AAC device was counterintuitive but essential - fewer options led to more actual use. Embedding communication teaching into daily routines was far more effective than isolated therapy sessions.

context.supportLevel: Tier 3 - high support with SLT and behaviour specialist involvement
